messages:
jamie: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide between a multiplexed regional front-door and keeping per-tenant proxies. multiplexing saves ENIs/IPs and infra cost but introduces authn/SNI complexity, src-ip preservation gaps, and wider blast radius. collecting tradeoffs and rollback ideas.

andrew: Multiplex for self-serve and mid tiers. ENI quotas are painful and customers keep requesting many subnets. pooling makes infra much cheaper. :+1:

sophia: Isolation is my top worry. One noisy tenant could affect dozens. We'll need tenant-level circuit breakers, strict QoS, and per-tenant observability to unblock PG/security reviews. :warning:

mike: From an ops/compliance POV per-tenant proxies are simpler for auditing and cert boundaries. But cost for small customers is hard to justify.

ellie: TLS: do we terminate at our relay or SNI-pass through to tenant endpoints? passthrough keeps tenant certs private but reduces our ability to do L7 routing and telemetry. hybrid might be the only practical compromise.

jamie: Spike findings: three modes feasible — `passthrough` (SNI->tenant backend), `terminate` (relay owns TLS, can mTLS to backend), `hybrid` (passthrough for enterprise, terminate for hosted). gaps: routing table scale, SNI cache eviction, NAT vs src-ip preservation.

andrew: Rollback story: front-door must support per-tenant kill-switch that flips the route to a 502 (fast fail) and an automated pin-to-dedicated-proxy action. Without that, cutovers will be slow and risky.

sophia: Observability needs: tenant-tagged traces at ingress, per-tenant error/latency dashboards, and alerts when a tenant drives frontend SLO regressions. also need audit trails for cert handling.

jamie: Perf tradeoffs: multiplexing adds an extra routing lookup but reduces backend cold-starts via pooled connections and shared KV prefix cache. CPU hotspot will be SNI lookup and connection multiplexor. We'll need a fast path in C for route lookup.

ellie: Source-IP preservation: NATing at relay preserves backend connectivity but loses true srcip for tenant logs or ACLs. Workaround: sign x-forwarded-for and include a token header with original IP. For customers needing real src, only dedicated ENI/pinning meets the requirement.

mike: Compliance asks often include pinned ENIs or private peering. Hybrid where enterprise gets pinned proxies while self-serve uses multiplexing seems pragmatic.

jamie: Proposed phased rollout: 1) implement multiplexed passthrough for self-serve (no cert mgmt), 2) add pinning pathway for enterprise (reserved ENI/proxy), 3) provide fast cutover runbook to re-pin tenants to dedicated proxies.

andrew: example policy prototype:
```
route {
  match: host:sni("tenant.example.com")
  mode: passthrough
  fallback: pin_to: "tenant-proxy-arn"
  circuit_breaker: 5xx_rate>3% -> isolate
}
```

jamie: Open questions for sign-off: - acceptable blast radius of multiplex layer? - SLA guarantees for pinned tenants? - minimum observability before enabling multiplex for >100 tenants?

sophia: Suggested guardrails before enabling multiplex broadly: tenant quotas, per-tenant circuit breakers, tokenized trace/header signing, and an API to instantly isolate a tenant. Without these it's too risky.

jamie: Action items: isolation spike (simulate noisy backend) -> andrew + ellie (due EOD next Friday). ops/backout playbook -> sophia + mike (draft mid-week). i'll write perf budget and SNI cache design doc.

deploy-bot: CI: multiplex-proxy-spike branch passed e2e smoke (image: rwd/multiplex-spike:canary). :tada:

jamie: i'll consolidate and put a follow-up RFC with the hybrid rollout and guardrails. shout if you object to hybrid as the enterprise default. :eyes:
